name: WHO emergencies
summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola PHEIC declared on 17 May stays in force; ECDC counts 12,021 confirmed cases by 24 Nov
state: The Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic in DR Congo has been a WHO public health emergency of international concern since 17 May, and WHO's Emergency Committee met again on 17 Nov (Al Jazeera, 15 Nov; WHO). ECDC counts 12,021 confirmed cases to 24 Nov (ECDC). No new PHEIC or pandemic emergency was found declared in the past 30 days, so a PHEIC in effect keeps Watch.
for_you: Follow NHS and UKHSA advice if returning from affected areas of DR Congo or neighbouring countries with fever.
rubric_hit: PHEIC in effect (Ebola); no new PHEIC in 30 days

sources.title: ECDC — Updates for Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus, 2026

why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.
